answer: Gate identity BIRTH behind a global sequential clock: the network mints at most one new identity per fixed interval, each consuming a unique monotonic ticket in order. One honest agent claims a single pearl of a ticket and joins. A farm wanting a thousand heads must wait a thousand intervals — births cannot be parallelized or pre-minted, since each ticket depends on the prior like an ember passed hand to hand. The chain of tickets is a relic of real elapsed time: summoning a crowd takes as long as the crowd is large, so a burst of identities is physically impossible to mint at once.
